passages.title: Ps. 122:1–2
passages.text: The song begins by remembering (**they said** is past tense) the invitation to go to Jerusalem for worship (**the house of the Lord**). The person has now arrived (**our feet have been standing**). The anticipation (**I was glad**) is now to be fulfilled.

passages.title: Ps. 122:3–5
passages.text: The singer looks around Jerusalem. **Bound firmly together** probably compares the physical coziness of the city to the sense of unity the pilgrim expects to find there.

passages.title: Ps. 122:6–9
passages.text: In light of what Jerusalem should be, the psalm ends by urging God’s people to seek the conditions that will make that a reality: **the peace of Jerusalem**.

notes.text: **Psalm** . This psalm celebrates Zion as God’s chosen city (compare Psalms 46 ; 48 ; 76 ; 87 ), and the privilege of going there on a pilgrimage (compare Psalm 84 ). Not only is “the house of the L ord ” there, but so are “the thrones of the house of David.”
